_comment: The rules step2cam's planning applies today, as they are in the code ("code" says where). Each decision in a plan's trace cites one by id@version. A rule's sources say whether it rests on a standard, recognised practice or step2cam's own judgement. Where a rule's logic is itself data, `data` names the file (and selector) in rulebase/rules/ that holds it.

rules.rationale: Compare independently planned and simulated available candidates in order: finishes the part; fewest distinct features left out; fewest setups; least extra stock thickness; shortest estimated machining time. Stable candidate order breaks exact ties. Finished means the holding route releases the outline and grip stock with no grip/travel omissions or failed execution checks; missing-tool operations do not change this status and each candidate reports its own tools_needed descriptions, features and operations. Unrelated unsupported details remain listed and ranked as features left out; it is not a dimensional or holding-force proof. Vise candidates require a dimensioned vise in the first mill. Fixture plate is withheld: screw-head/tool clearance, supported seating and transfer of residual stock are not implemented; no simulated plate holding is claimed. For unavailable-row eligibility only, step2cam judgement requires two unthreaded Z-axis through holes of 3.2–9 mm diameter spread at least 25% of the XY bounding-box diagonal; otherwise report no suitable through holes. No new machine workholding kind is introduced until this can be validated. Margins and tabs await #87.

sources.ref: Judgement: lexicographic choosing policy approved in #94; full comparison uses the same motion length/feed time estimate as the page, excluding setup and tool-change labour.

rules.rationale: Vise flip candidate: trace availability separately; setup.workholding chooses among simulated candidates. When selected, solve sacrificial grip stock, verify finished side bands and edge seating against the mesh, then face to thickness. Refuse unsupported geometry or reach; #94 may offer or withhold this option independently.

sources.ref: Judgement: 1 mm facing allowance; existing grip and clearance rules; numerical stock rounding upward to 0.0001 mm. Contact and support fractions, inboard search and numerical tolerances are judgement documented in rules/workholding.json and docs/capp-plan.md.

rules.rationale: A tapped answer is threaded only for an ISO 261 coarse size this table lists, or a size with an explicit pitch (M10x1.25); an explicit pitch is taken as given, not checked against ISO 261's fine pitches.
A tapped answer whose full-thread depth (its @depth, or the hole.full_thread answer that overrides it) cannot be read is not threaded.
A tapped answer for a feature the part no longer has is not threaded.
A thread the file marks without a size is not threaded: answer it in Specify.

A blind thread deeper than its hole is not threaded. The full-thread depth is the one asked for (Specify's hole.full_thread answer, which takes precedence over a tapped answer's @depth, as in specify-core; else that @depth), else specify-core's default: the drill depth less three pitches, rounded down to 0.5 mm, at least one pitch. The plan marks a default depth (default_depth) so a tap may cut less of it (tool.thread.tap_or_mill); an asked depth is never shortened.

sources.note: specify-core's default minimum full thread

rules.rationale: The part's material is Specify's answer (part.material), unless the resources override it (overrides.material). It is placed in an ISO 513 group by the whole words of its name; a printed material or a name nothing matches gets no group, and the tools' own cutting data are used. A stand-in until specify-core gives the material's family.

sources.note: the six groups
placing a material by the words of its name, a stand-in

rules.rationale: The stock is the part's box grown by the margins: top and bottom stock along the roughing direction, the margin across it. The roughing setup is zeroed on the stock, the others on the part's box.
A hole is cut from the first setup, roughing's first, whose axis it lies along and from which no part material stands above its opening.
A hole with part material above its opening from every setup it lies along cannot be reached by a three-axis tool.
A hole whose axis is along none of the six setup directions needs a setup this bridge does not make.
The stock above the part's top is faced off first.
Roughing clears the stock down to the part's mesh, leaving a web below the part, from the roughing setup.
Roughing is not planned when faces did not triangulate: a mesh with holes in it would let roughing cut into the part.
Roughing is not planned when the mesh strays from the curved faces by more than camlib accepts (0.1 mm).
The upward flat faces between the top and the roughing floor are finished, as roughing's layers can leave up to a stepdown on them.
Holes of one diameter, depth and ending are one operation over their centres.
Counterbores and spotfaces of one size are one operation, cut after the holes.
Internal threads of one size are thread-milled down the bore from its top: all of it for a through hole, else the full-thread depth.

sources.note: coarse pitches
specify-core's default minimum full thread
thread milling rather than tapping, through holes threaded their whole depth

rules.rationale: A closed slot with round ends is cut to size as an operation of its own.
A rectangular slot, pocket or notch is cut with its model corner radii; an open side runs out past the part. Matching upright corner fillets and section recesses belong to that operation.
A V-channel is cut by running a sharp V-bit along it with its tip on the root.
An outside wall of upright planes and cylinders is finished down to its floor by a contour after roughing.

A wall finishing contour around a convex outline comes down one cutter radius before the start of its loop and leads onto the wall along its tangent, and leaves it the same way, so the cutter neither plunges nor stops against the finished wall. camlib's contour takes straight tangent leads only (lead_in_mm, lead_out_mm), not arcs, starts the loop where it chooses, and refuses a lead that cuts into the part. Only on a convex outline is every tangent of the tool path clear of the part, so any other outline is plunged at the wall with no lead, as before. The job's wall finishing note cites this rule.

sources.note: judgement: one radius takes the plunge off the wall; an arc lead would be the usual choice where camlib offers one

rules.rationale: An outside wall that is not upright planes and cylinders keeps its roughing allowance.
Modelled equal-leg 45° top loops are chamfered with their wall or bore at size. Convex top edge rounds retain the chamfer meeting their middle.

A convex edge round whose faces are not all cylinders along the roughing setup's axis (a horizontal round, not a vertical corner) is not cut by roughing or a wall and stays sharp; one on the top face may still be cut as an edge chamfer, which then replaces this decision.
Chamfers without a complete reachable equal-leg 45° top loop and a wall or bore at size stay out with their geometry reason and a hand-chamfer instruction. Geometry refusals do not request tools.
Countersinks are not planned.
Turned features are made on a lathe.
A thread on a hole that is not cut is not cut either.

rules.warning_label: holes stop short of far face
rules.rationale: A through hole that ends short of the part's far face may have something between (a counterbore or chamfer at the far end, a shoulder) that is not planned.

A feature with no operation of its own, none of whose flat faces points away from the roughing setup, is taken as covered by roughing (a heuristic); where flats or walls do not reach it, it keeps the roughing allowance.
A feature with no operation of its own that faces away from the roughing setup is not planned.
Without the mesh nothing is roughed, so a feature with no operation of its own is not cut.
A feature with no operation of its own is not cut when roughing is not planned.
Without the mesh, hole approaches and what lies beyond through holes are not checked against the part.

In each setup: facing, roughing, flats, holes, counterbores, slots, notches and V-channels, walls, edge chamfers, then threads last, as nothing should cut near a finished thread and the stock is compared with the part just before them.
A contour knows only its outline: a wall is finished only after roughing has cleared the stock beside it.
A wall standing on a flat is finished only if that flat is cut.
A wall is finished with roughing's end mill; with none it is not finished.

rules.warning_label: outside walls too narrow to finish
rules.rationale: The room beside a wall must take the end mill and the roughing allowance on whatever stands opposite: the library's radial_allowance_mm (0.3 mm by default) or twice the mesh's error, whichever is more.
A V-channel cut in a flat is cut only if that flat is cut.
A V-channel needs a sharp V-bit no wider than its angle.
The V-bit must state its stepdown.
The room beside a V-channel must take the bit's half-width beyond the channel's.
Flats follow roughing with the same end mill: without roughing they are not cut.
An outside chamfer is cut only if its wall is finished to size; otherwise the edge stays sharp and a modelled chamfer is left for hand finishing.
A mouth chamfer runs only after every hole or slot it depends on has a tool. A combined round-as-chamfer operation is blocked as a whole if any opening cannot be cut.
Facing and roughing use the end mill the library names for them (facing_tool, roughing_tool), else the largest end mill.
Flats are cut with roughing's end mill, after roughing.

A hole is drilled with the largest drill not larger than it and at most drill_tolerance_mm under it; else bored by helix with the largest end mill that fits with room to helix. Drill flutes must also reach from the stock top through full breakthrough, plus the candidate point height and camlib numerical guard; this conservatively includes the point even for tip-referenced bottoms and does not shorten reach for exit obstructions.
A counterbore is bored with the largest end mill that fits it with room to helix.
The largest thread mill whose pitch range takes the pitch, that fits the drilled hole, whose neck clears the crests and that reaches the thread's bottom.
An operation uses its tool's cutting data (feed, speed, plunge, stepdown, stepover), with what the tool states for the material's ISO 513 group in their place.

sources.note: tool makers give cutting data by ISO 513 workpiece group
the values themselves are the shop's, in resources.json

rules.rationale: A round-ended slot is cut with the largest end mill narrower than it.

rules.warning_label: corner radii larger than the model
rules.rationale: A rectangular recess keeps the model outline. If the chosen cutter radius exceeds the model corner radius, report the larger inside corner radii as a plan deviation; no corner relief is requested by today's analysis or answers.

A sharp V-bit narrower than the channel, run with its tip on the root, leaves a wedge of stock on each wall. Its width across the top is the channel's half-width less the bit's half-width at the channel's depth, (width - tip diameter) / 2 - depth × tan(bit angle / 2); above 0.005 mm the channel is reported as partly cut with that stock left, as wider notch corners are.
A notch is cut with the largest end mill narrower than it whose flutes reach its depth.
The widest sharp V-bit whose included angle is no more than the channel's: a wider angle would cut its walls, a flat tip could not reach the root.
A wall is finished with roughing's end mill.
The largest 90° chamfer mill covering the whole width plus tip clearance, within loop clearance and cutting-length reach from the stock top.
An operation the execution engine refuses is left out, its features say why, and the plan is finished again without it.
When roughing is refused, nothing is covered by it: its features are not cut.
Each setup is cut on the resources' mill, the first machine of kind mill. With no machine described, its travels, tool holding and tool changer are not checked.

rules.rationale: Single plunge through 3 diameters; beyond that full-retract pecks of half a diameter, capped by a positive library peck_mm. Full retract is used even at intermediate depths because drills have no through-tool coolant declaration. Depth is measured from where the drill enters, not the stock top: after roughing, the hole's mouth when the roughing cutter with its radial allowance fits the hole, or when a flats pass at the mouth's height sweeps the whole disc over it (the cutter outreaches the hole by at least half its stepover); otherwise the lowest roughing layer (stepping down from its top) that keeps the bottom allowance above the mouth, since a cutter too big for the hole cannot clear the disc over it; without roughing, the stock top as faced; and the top of any slot, notch or V-channel whose floor it is in, as those are cut after holes. Above the reference deep-hole threshold (5D), warn and trace the hole identity and ratio: pilot plus deep-hole drilling is not planned, so full-retract pecking remains the fallback.

sources.note: Conservative constant increment and full retract without a per-drill through-tool coolant declaration.

rules.rationale: Stopgap for stevecad/camlib#122: each roughing layer is checked against depth below the stock top. Cap at min(flute length, stickout) minus 1 mm, clearing numerical guards and keeping the flute end and holder face above stock. Relax the flute limit to holder clearance once camlib checks per-layer cutting depth. Features must be fully reached; needed-tool queries include this margin in both flute length and stickout. Flats below the cap and wholly unreachable wall bands are left out; crossing wall bands are finished down to the cap, warning of the allowance left below. Dependent chamfers follow missing walls and V-channels on uncleared flats are left out.

sources.note: https://github.com/stevecad/camlib/issues/122

rules.rationale: Grip the stock long sides across the narrower XY dimension (X on a tie). Use at least 3.175 mm and 20% of stock height, no more than 50%; leave 1 mm above the jaws for side cutting. These values are step2cam judgement, not a sourced minimum for standard vise jaws or a holding-force calculation. With specified parallels the grip is jaw height minus parallels height. Without parallels_height_mm, raise stock on parallels or similar so the jaws grip only the chosen height; that support is not modeled or checked, so through cuts are not checked against it. Jaw thickness is conservatively modeled equal to jaw height because resources do not yet describe thickness. Per-setup resources.overrides.clamping proposals select an axis, grip and optional parallels; validate them by the same dimensional and clearance checks, and trace them as given. Audit later stock-face grip bands against earlier retained, tooled operations after caps and exclusions, using rotation/origin transforms and conservative cut envelopes. Warn on possible overlap or missing information; the audit is not a stock simulation or a proof of face retention or holding strength.
rules.code: workholding.rs clamp, validate_overrides; settle.rs cap_roughing; clamping_history.rs check

sources.note: The 3.175 mm minimum, 20% minimum and 50% maximum grip, 1 mm clearance, and square jaw sections are planning judgement; no applicable public source for the minimum grip of standard vise jaws was found.

rules.rationale: Spot only twist drills, including tap drills, before drilling, grouped by tool per setup. Indexable insert drills start on their own and are not spotted (no such tool type here). Ordinary spots require point angle >= twist drill angle; enlarged countersinks instead require only the countersink angle match (the twist-drill angle minimum is disabled). This enlarged-countersink exception is a reviewer decision. Depth = (spot diameter / 2) / tan(point angle / 2), referenced to the tip. Prefer the smallest covering tool; no undersize fallback, since it cannot make the requested spot or countersink. A countersink is cut only when the tool covers its larger diameter and matches its included angle within 1°. No peck; 0.2 s dwell for a clean spot/chamfer. Insertion precedes exclusion replay; subsequent pruning never recreates a refused spot.

sources.ref: Harvey Performance, Spot Drilling: The First Step to Precision Drilling
sources.note: Read 2026-11-08: a larger point angle lets the centre engage first; equal angles are acceptable. Spot drills can chamfer hole mouths. Manufacturer replies recommend a larger tool plunged only to the desired drill diameter.

sources.ref: MSC Industrial Supply, Spotting & Step Drills, Countersinks & Center Reamers Technical Information
sources.note: Read 2026-11-08: spotting establishes a true centre; choose a point angle equal to or greater than the final drill. Lists 120° spots for 118° or 120° drills.

rules.warning_label: operations left out for want of a tool
rules.rationale: After tool resolution, an operation no tool in the library cuts is taken out of its setup rather than listed with no tool: each feature it would cut is skipped with why and the tool it needs, and an operation with no feature of its own warns that it is left out. The operations after it are numbered again, as after an exclusion; tools_needed still names it as it was numbered before. Roughing that does not run covers nothing. Supplied choices and execution-engine exclusions name operations as the finished plan numbers them.

Spot drilling no tool cuts is taken out; its holes are still drilled, so they are not skipped: one warning per setup names them, says how many holes are drilled without spotting and which spot drill is needed.

Each requirement in Specify's answers that the plan does not act on is named, with where it applies: fits, the general tolerance, surface finish, edge, coating and heat-treatment notes, datum flatness and controls, and position, location and runout tolerances (grouped, one warning each). Nothing is machined differently because of them. The material, tapped threads and their full-thread depth, and clearance holes cut to their drawn size are acted on and not warned of; datums and how holes are located are choices, not requirements. Answers Specify did not ask given the other answers (datum flatness and controls, positions and runouts under part.locating '± dimensions'; ± locations under 'position tolerances'; a position on a general-function hole) write nothing on the drawing and are not warned of.

sources.ref: Project review M1: drawing requirements were silently ignored (an H7 bore drilled with no finishing pass, flatness, position tolerances and Ra 3.2 unmentioned); the smallest fix is one warning per requirement not acted on.

rules.rationale: Supplied choices must pass the same checks as ruled choices. Refuse unacceptable or unsupported choices and use the rule choice.

Prefer a matching M3–M6 tap in ISO N material; check hand, pre-drill, blind/through, chamfer plus one pitch clearance and stock-top reach. Otherwise use the unchanged thread-mill selector. Size/material cutoff is step2cam judgement. The default blind full thread (drill depth less three pitches) leaves less than a form C tap's three-pitch lead plus one pitch, so a library tap could never cut it: when the depth is the default, not asked for, the tap cuts the drilled full-diameter depth less its own chamfer lead and one pitch, rounded down to 0.5 mm as the default is, if that is shorter, and is refused only below one pitch. An asked depth (hole.full_thread or tapped @depth) is checked unchanged and refused if the tap cannot reach it. This is a step2cam decision (review M7); the default itself stays specify-core's.

sources.ref: reference/tap-drills.json: sourced drill table and form formula, explicit M3–M6 / ISO N shop policy

rules.rationale: Finish a wall in one full-depth pass where the flute reaches, otherwise the fewest equal passes no deeper than its flute length. This axial finishing policy does not inherit roughing stepdown; camlib reach and stock-contact checks remain mandatory.

sources.note: finishing the radial allowance after roughing, not clearing full-width stock

rules.rationale: When spindle.collet_change is manual and a setup selects more than one shank size, report operator intervention independently of ATC pocket capacity; make no tool substitutions.

sources.note: machine capability and selected tool shank dimensions from resources

rules.rationale: Roughing clears each layer in parallel raster passes at the end mill's stepover (at most half its diameter), joined by the shortest routing camlib offers. The job's roughing note cites this rule.

sources.note: judgement: one simple clearing pattern for every part; no adaptive or offset clearing is chosen

rules.rationale: Roughing keeps its tool centre within one cutter radius and 1 mm of the setup's stock, so no pass runs far out in the air beside it; the stock edge is still cut, and a pass can still start beside the stock. The 1 mm lets camlib prove a link along the stock's edge clear of the stock, so it is fed at the cutting feed rather than the entry feed. camlib's own roughing region is the stock grown by four times the tool's reach, which raster passes and links sweep through at feed. The job's roughing note cites this rule.

sources.note: judgement: material is only ever within one radius of the stock box, so a tool centre farther out cuts nothing

rules.rationale: Roughing leaves the library's radial_allowance_mm on the walls and bottom_allowance_mm on the floors (0.3 and 0.2 mm when the library gives none), each at least twice the mesh's surface error, so roughing to a mesh that strays from the part never cuts into the part. Flats, walls, bores, slots and notches cut to size with no allowance. The job's roughing note cites this rule.

sources.note: judgement: the default allowances are step2cam's, not a maker's recommendation; libraries state their own

rules.rationale: Roughing enters each layer from outside the stock where it can, otherwise by a helix; slots and notches enter by a helix. Every helix ramps at 3°. The job's notes cite this rule where a roughing, slot or notch uses it.

sources.note: judgement: one shallow ramp for every tool and material; not taken from any tool's cutting data

rules.rationale: A tool whose library entry gives no flutes is sent to camlib with two for a drill or spot drill and three for any other tool, the values step2cam sent before libraries could say. camlib checks the count and does not use it to cut. The job's notes name each tool given the default.

sources.note: judgement: kept so that a library without flute counts plans as before; no flute count is guessed for a library tool

rules.rationale: A tool whose library entry gives no material is sent to camlib as carbide, the value step2cam sent before libraries could say. camlib does not use it to cut. The job's notes name each tool given the default.

sources.note: judgement: kept so that a library without tool materials plans as before; no material is guessed for a library tool
